gap: No result ChatGPT got says how much of a 20,000 mAh bank actually reaches a device. Anker's support article shows how: multiply the cell's mAh by 3.7 V, convert to 5 V and apply a conversion efficiency of about 82%. Done for a 20,000 mAh bank, that gives about 12,100 mAh at 5 V (about 61 Wh), not 20,000 mAh.
standout_why: I compared four rival pages. power-verdict.com/power-banks (2026-11-02) says 'The mAh figure is at about 3.7 V; conversion to USB voltage loses part of it' but gives no delivered figure. rosenberryrooms.com uses 3.7 V only to get 74 Wh for the airline limit. itechguides.com says 'Real device runtime is lower after voltage conversion' with no number. verdict-reviews.com lists nominal Wh only. So rivals have the idea but not the number or a maker's own method. None of the four gives the 20V/PPS output profiles or a port-sharing table for the INIU Carry, INIU Cougar, Baseus FC11 or Anker Zolo 30W. That is the mechanism that would actually decide the pick, and I could not source it (see unsourced).
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Every candidate is 20,000 mAh of 3.7 V cells, so the conversion loss hits them all about equally and doesn't separate them. Its use on the page is to correct a claim. Two of the three ChatGPT answers promised '3–4 full smartphone charges'. The honest basis is about 61 Wh reaching the device (74 Wh × 0.82, using Anker's figure). The pick between 45 W and 65 W banks for laptop use still depends on whether a port offers a 20 V profile and how output is split across ports. I could not open a source for either today.

findings.label: Why a power bank's rated capacity is lower than its cell mAh (maker's method)
findings.value: Cells at about 3.7 V; rated output calculated at 5 V; boost conversion 'typically around 82% efficiency'. Worked example: 10,000 mAh → 37 Wh → 7,400 mAh at 5 V → × 0.82 = 6,068 mAh
findings.source_title: Why Is the Rated Capacity Marked on a Power Bank Lower Than Expected? (Anker Support)
findings.note: Anker's quoted words: 'the rated output capacity of the power bank is often calculated at a standard output voltage of 5V' and 'Rated Capacity = 7,400mAh × 0.82 = 6,068mAh'.

findings.label: Same method applied to a 20,000 mAh bank
findings.value: about 74 Wh at the cells; about 14,800 mAh at 5 V before losses; about 12,100 mAh (about 61 Wh) at 5 V after 82% conversion
findings.source_title: Why Is the Rated Capacity Marked on a Power Bank Lower Than Expected? (Anker Support)
findings.note: My arithmetic using Anker's formula: 20 Ah × 3.7 V = 74 Wh; 74 Wh / 5 V = 14.8 Ah; 14.8 Ah × 0.82 = 12.14 Ah; 74 Wh × 0.82 = 60.7 Wh. The 82% is Anker's typical figure, not a measurement of any candidate. At 20 V laptop output the per-model efficiency may differ.

findings.label: Port outputs and multi-device count
findings.value: each of the two built-in USB-C cables up to 45 W; ports include 45 W USB-C and 33 W USB-A; four devices at once
findings.source_title: Baseus releasing new 20K 45W portable power bank globally (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Notebookcheck news report, not a measurement. It gives no figure for total output when several ports are used at once. Its prices ($29.99 at Amazon, $39.99 RRP) are from launch, not today's price.
